statusText: Roughly 90 minutes after the Friday U.S. cash close (20:00 UTC) and approaching the CME weekend halt (~22:00 UTC): the confirmed drivers already known this session -- the August UMich sentiment miss (51.0 vs ~54.5 consensus), the July Retail Sales drop (-0.6% MoM), and Broadcom (-4.1% to $395.31) / Applied Materials (-5%) weakness on margin-mix and post-rally-valuation concerns -- remain fully digested with no new escalation. Since the prior run, AMD's previously conflicting reporting has resolved decisively: AMD closed up about 6.5% to $514.13 on its well-received bond issuance and growth commentary, alongside firm SanDisk and Western Digital, reinforcing that today's semis-sector moves are earnings-specific single-name dispersion rather than a coherent directional move. Reporting on the Nasdaq's own close is inconsistent across sources (one snippet shows the Composite +0.17%, another shows -0.3%, with the S&P 500 and Dow both around -0.2%), underscoring the mixed rather than directional character of the session. NQ futures continue trading within the broad multi-hour range established earlier in the session; precise-tick sourcing remains inconsistent across search snippets and no source describes a failed-pullback or repeated-extension reaction. VIX holds calm near 14.6. The 10-year Treasury yield holds near 4.70% (+5bp) and the 2-year near 4.17% (+3bp), with reporting attributing the move to the soft retail sales print plus incremental (not escalatory) U.S. rhetoric that its naval blockade of Iranian ports could continue "indefinitely." WTI holds flat near $81.3. On the Strait of Hormuz, no new discrete escalation has emerged since the prior run -- the confirmed Thursday-evening two-tanker ADNOC attack plus a separate drone strike on an exiting tanker remain the latest confirmed incidents, with regional condemnations already priced in as ongoing background risk. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily quota remained exhausted this run (one call plus one retry, both rate_limit errors), so this run again relies entirely on WebSearch, with reasonable cross-source corroboration on individual stock moves, VIX, yields and oil, but continued inconsistency on the exact NQ tick and the exact Nasdaq Composite close.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Tail eases to 6% (still low) from 9% last hour as the session winds down toward the Friday close/weekend halt with the day's known drivers fully digested and AMD's prior ambiguity resolved higher, and with no failed-pullback or repeated-extension structure identified in NQ itself. Stress eases to 34% (moderate) from 41% as the cash session ends and today's semis-earnings dispersion stops actively repricing, though it stays in the moderate band rather than dropping sharply given the still-open cross-currents (yields up modestly, standing Hormuz risk, inconsistent index-level close reporting). Confidence eases slightly to 40% (medium-low) from 43% on the continued Alpha Vantage outage and conflicting reports on the exact Nasdaq close, offset by good corroboration on the individual stock moves, yields and oil. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active regardless of the current EA_ON state. An upgrade to a higher Tail state would require an observed failed-pullback/repeated-extension reaction in NQ itself -- not the standing semis dispersion, yield drift, or Hormuz coverage on their own.
headline: AMD's prior ambiguity resolves sharply higher (+6.5%) alongside firm SanDisk/Western Digital, offsetting confirmed Broadcom (-4.1%) and Applied Materials (-5%) weakness as the Friday session heads into the close and CME weekend halt; VIX stays calm (~14.6), NQ holds its established range with no failed-pullback structure, and reporting on the exact Nasdaq close stays inconsistent, keeping the tape mixed rather than directional.

lookbackSummary: Tail held in the low band (7-16%) through the trailing 24 hours, easing from Thursday evening's post-CPI/PPI digestion into a stable single-digit floor through Friday's Asian/European session, then holding 7-9% through today's confirmed UMich/Retail Sales misses and the Broadcom/Applied Materials semis drag, before easing further to 6% this hour as AMD's prior ambiguity resolved higher and the session approached the close. Stress ran from the upper-30s Thursday evening down to a low of 23% in the early Friday Asian session, rebuilt through the European morning and the confirmed UMich print (peaking near 44%), held roughly 40-41% through the U.S. afternoon, then eased to 34% this hour as the cash session ended, with the standing Strait of Hormuz crisis providing a persistent, contained event-importance driver throughout. No published assessment exists for the 20:00 UTC hour (a run did not publish in that window).
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to stay low (2-6%) through the next 24 hours: it holds near 6% into the CME weekend halt (~22:00 UTC) as today's digested drivers stop actively repricing, then drops to a low weekend floor (~2%) once NQ futures enter the halt and stays there through the entire 24-hour horizon, which remains within the weekend (CME resumes Sunday around 22:00 UTC, beyond this window). Stress is projected to fall sharply from today's moderate band as the cash session ends, then decay toward a low single-digit weekend floor (~7%) held there by the absence of any active session rather than a resolved risk picture -- the standing Strait of Hormuz crisis remains the principal source of weekend headline/gap risk into Sunday's reopen. No forecast slot currently implies an action change from EA_ON. Confidence is projected to decay gradually from the high-30s toward the mid-20s as the horizon moves away from this run's live evidence and, further out, away from any live trading session at all.
